FINDING 7 — the JS backend does not bounds-check a slice index. The C backend
panics; JS silently yields 0 and exits 0.

FILE: js_slice_index_no_bounds_check.zen.txt   (xs has 3 elements, index is 5)
CMD:  ./zen run     tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/js_slice_index_no_bounds_check.zen.txt
OUT:  zen: panic: slice index out of bounds
      rc 134                                   (correct — this is the language
                                                guarantee: OOB index PANICS)
CMD:  ./zen emit-js tests/fixtures/zen/fuzz-repro/js_slice_index_no_bounds_check.zen.txt | node
OUT:  0
      rc 0                                     (no panic, no diagnostic)

NOTE the C preamble has `zen__idx` (src/compiler/backend/c/c_emit.zen:260) which
      does the check; the JS emitter has no equivalent. Divide-by-zero IS
      checked on both backends (JS prints "zen: panic: integer divide by zero"),
      so this is a gap in one guard, not in the whole JS panic story.

CLASS: C/JS divergence + a safety guarantee that one backend does not honour.
      Invisible to tools/fuzz-diff.zen for the same reason as FINDING 6: the
      C side exits 134, which is classified C-FAIL and skipped.
FOUND BY: hand-directed panic-parity probing.
